hints.title: Consecutive Runs
hints.text: A balanced substring consists of a continuous run of zeros followed immediately by a continuous run of ones.

hints.title: Run Measurement
hints.text: Count the number of consecutive zeros and subsequent ones for each transition boundary.

hints.title: Balance Doubling
hints.text: The maximum balanced length from a paired run is twice the minimum of the zeros count and ones count.

hints.title: Reference Implementation
hints.text:
```python
class Solution:
    def findTheLongestBalancedSubstring(self, s: str) -> int:
        max_len = 0
        n = len(s)
        i = 0
        while i < n:
            zeros = 0
            while i < n and s[i] == '0':
                zeros += 1
                i += 1
            ones = 0
            while i < n and s[i] == '1':
                ones += 1
                i += 1
            max_len = max(max_len, 2 * min(zeros, ones))
        return max_len
```

variables: N: length of binary string s
complexity.notes: Single pass counting consecutive zero and one segments.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Checking all substrings naively takes cubic or quadratic time.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Linear scan counting contiguous blocks of zeros followed by ones.
